meta.topic: Creating Your First Repository & The Three-Stage Workflow

questions.question: Which command initializes a new Git repository in the current directory?
questions.explanation: `git init` creates an empty Git repository by generating a hidden `.git` folder in your project root.

questions.question: What hidden folder does Git use to store all its tracking metadata and commit history?
questions.explanation: The `.git` directory contains the object database, commit history, branch references, and configuration for that repository.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of the three main areas in Git?
questions.explanation: Files are edited in your Working Directory, prepared for commit in the Staging Area (index), and saved permanently into the Repository.

questions.question: Which command checks which files are modified, staged, or untracked?
questions.explanation: `git status` provides a comprehensive overview of your working tree and staging area.

questions.question: What does the command `git add index.html` do?

options.A: Creates a new file named index.html
options.B: Moves changes in index.html to the staging area
options.C: Immediately commits index.html to repository history

questions.explanation: `git add` adds the current state of a file to the staging area so it can be included in the next commit.

questions.question: What does `git add .` do?

options.B: Stages all new and modified files in the current directory and subdirectories
options.C: Initializes a repository in the parent folder
options.D: Commits all changes with a default message

questions.explanation: The dot `.` represents the current directory, staging all tracked modifications and untracked files under the current path.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the `-m` flag in `git commit -m "Add navbar"`?

options.B: Specify the commit message directly in the command

questions.explanation: The `-m` flag supplies the commit message inline without opening a text editor like Vim or nano.

questions.question: If a file is listed under 'Untracked files' in `git status`, what does it mean?

options.A: Git has detected a merge conflict
options.B: The file exists in your directory but Git is not monitoring its changes yet
options.C: The file has been deleted from GitHub

questions.explanation: Untracked files are files in your working directory that have never been added to Git via `git add`.

questions.question: Why does Git use a Staging Area instead of committing all file changes directly?

options.A: To compress the files before saving
options.B: To allow you to pick and choose exactly which changes belong together in a logical commit
options.C: Because hard drives cannot write files directly

questions.explanation: The staging area allows you to craft atomic, meaningful commits rather than dumping unrelated file edits into one messy snapshot.

questions.question: What does `git commit -a -m "message"` (or `-am`) do for an untracked file?

options.A: It automatically stages and commits both tracked and untracked files
options.B: It only commits previously tracked, modified files — it ignores brand-new untracked files

questions.explanation: The `-a` flag only auto-stages files that Git is already tracking. Brand-new untracked files still require explicit `git add`.
